key_insight: CCL reduces teacher bias in LLM distillation by alternating source-domain calibration with target-domain student learning, and it provably drives the student toward the oracle policy without needing target-domain reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical distillation recipe for shifting data distributions, where reliable target labels or rewards are unavailable but robust student performance is still required.
method: Calibrate the teacher using token-level branching and reward feedback from source questions only.
Train the student on target questions with the calibrated teacher as the supervision signal.
Feed the updated student back into later calibration rounds to progressively reduce bias.
evidence_signal: In an autoregressive policy setting, the paper proves polynomial-rate convergence of the student’s expected average KL divergence to the oracle student, and shows a separation from regularized direct matching.
watch_item: The guarantee depends on iterative calibration-learning dynamics and source-domain reward feedback, so performance may degrade if the source feedback is noisy or the source-target shift is extreme.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
